Gram-negative cells appear pink or red at the end of Gram staining because of the counterstain, safranin. After the initial steps, Gram-negative cells lose the crystal violet-iodine complex because they have a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane. Finally, safranin is applied as the counterstain, which stains these cells pink or red under the microscope.

Demand for rice is elastic because the quantity demanded falls by a larger percentage (25%) than the price increase (10%). This results in an elasticity coefficient of -2.5. When demand is elastic, a price increase will actually lower the total revenue for the seller.

Cassava must be processed to reduce the hazard of hydrogen cyanide, which is released when the plant tissue is damaged. Processing, such as grating the roots for garri, breaks the cells so that the enzyme linamarase can act on linamarin. Furthermore, roasting the mash drives off much of the remaining hydrogen cyanide. Sun-drying thin chips also lowers the cyanide content. This processing is necessary because poorly processed cassava has been linked to konzo, a paralytic disease.
